cards.hypothesis: Inter-subject variability in autonomic nervous system baseline tone causes systematic shifts in prediction interval widths across subjects, violating the exchangeability assumption when calibration pools heterogeneous subjects.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with high sympathetic baseline tone exhibit higher heart rate variability (HRV) dispersion, leading to wider conformity scores during calibration; when applied to low-tone subjects, intervals become anti-conservative.
cards.causal_path: Baseline sympathetic tone (LF/HF ratio) -> HRV dispersion (SDNN) -> conformity score distribution quantiles -> prediction interval coverage
control_variables: Stratify calibration by LF/HF ratio tertiles
Match age and medication status across folds
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is driven by sensor noise floor differences across recording devices rather than physiology.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deviation correlates with device model SNR specifications, not with LF/HF ratio.
cards.distinguishing_test: Within same device model, regress coverage error on LF/HF ratio controlling for SNR; significant physiology coefficient supports H1.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows LF/HF ratio explains ~15-25% of HRV variance; conformity score dispersion scales with HRV variance.
minimum_data_needed: Ground truth labels for target variable (e.g., arrhythmia events)
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in highest LF/HF tertile show >10% coverage drop when calibrated on pooled data vs. stratified calibration.
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between LF/HF ratio and coverage error after device-stratified analysis (p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_error ~ LF_HF_tertile + (1|device) + age + medication; test fixed effect of tertile.
cards.falsification_test: Synthetic data where conformity scores are generated independent of LF/HF but with device-specific noise; H1 mechanism should not reproduce observed coverage pattern.

cards.hypothesis: Electrode-skin impedance drift during long recordings creates segment-dependent signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) degradation, altering conformity score distributions non-uniformly across time.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Impedance increases cause baseline wander and high-frequency attenuation, reducing R-peak detection accuracy in later segments; this inflates conformity scores for noise-contaminated segments, widening intervals spuriously.
cards.causal_path: Electrode impedance (kOhm) -> R-peak detection F1 score -> RR interval error distribution -> conformity score quantiles -> coverage
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage drift is caused by physiological non-stationarity (e.g., circadian HRV changes), not sensor degradation.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage error correlates with time-of-day features, not with measured impedance.
cards.distinguishing_test: Partial correlation of coverage error with impedance controlling for time-of-day; significant impedance partial correlation supports H2.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Impedance >10 kOhm can degrade R-peak F1 by >30% in ambulatory ECG; conformity scores directly use RR intervals.
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with impedance >15 kOhm show coverage exceeding nominal by >15% due to inflated conformity scores.
cards.failure_condition: Impedance and coverage error uncorrelated after controlling for movement artifacts (p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Segment-level regression: coverage_deviation ~ impedance + movement_flag + time_of_day; test impedance coefficient.
cards.falsification_test: Inject synthetic impedance-correlated noise into clean data; if coverage pattern differs from real data, mechanism is insufficient.

cards.hypothesis: Circadian modulation of heart rate variability violates the i.i.d. assumption across day/night segments, causing conformal prediction calibrated on daytime data to under-cover at night.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Parasympathetic dominance at night increases HRV complexity (higher sample entropy), shifting conformity score distribution toward higher values; daytime-calibrated quantiles are too low for nighttime segments.
cards.causal_path: Circadian phase (core body temperature minimum) -> autonomic balance (HF power) -> HRV sample entropy -> conformity score distribution -> coverage
control_variables: Align segments to individual CBTmin via actigraphy
cards.rival_explanation: Nighttime coverage drop is due to reduced movement artifact at night, not circadian physiology.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage error correlates with actigraphy-measured movement, not circadian phase.
cards.distinguishing_test: Within NREM sleep (low movement), test if coverage error still correlates with circadian phase.
cards.effect_size_rationale: HF power varies 2-3 fold day vs night; sample entropy changes ~0.2-0.3 units; conformity scores scale with entropy.
minimum_data_needed: Core body temperature or melatonin for circadian phase
cards.testable_prediction: Night segments (0-4h post CBTmin) show >8% under-coverage when calibrated on day segments (8-12h post CBTmin).
cards.failure_condition: No coverage difference between circadian-matched and mismatched calibration after sleep-stage stratification.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired t-test: coverage_day_calibrated_on_day vs coverage_night_calibrated_on_day; mixed model with circadian phase as continuous predictor.
cards.falsification_test: Phase-randomized surrogate RR intervals preserving power spectrum but destroying circadian structure; if coverage pattern persists, circadian mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Temporal concept drift in the target physiological state (e.g., progressive ischemia) causes the label-feature relationship to shift, making calibration conformity scores non-exchangeable with test segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Progressive ST-segment deviation alters the morphology features used for prediction; conformity scores computed on early stable segments underestimate dispersion in later ischemic segments.
cards.causal_path: Ischemia severity (ST deviation mm) -> morphology feature distribution (PCA of beat templates) -> nonconformity score (distance to class prototype) -> coverage
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability stems from increasing noise during ischemic episodes, not label-feature drift.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage error correlates with signal quality index, not ST deviation magnitude.
cards.distinguishing_test: In high-SQI segments only, test correlation between ST deviation and coverage error.
cards.effect_size_rationale: ST deviation >1mm changes QRS/T-wave morphology substantially; nonconformity scores based on morphology are highly sensitive.
minimum_data_needed: Continuous ECG with expert ST annotations
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with ST deviation >2mm show coverage <80% when calibrated on <0.5mm segments (nominal 90%).
cards.failure_condition: Coverage stable across ST deviation strata after controlling for SQI.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression of coverage on ST deviation controlling for SQI; test slope at 0.5 quantile.
cards.falsification_test: Permute ST deviation labels across segments; if coverage-ST relationship persists, mechanism is spurious.

cards.hypothesis: Inconsistent annotation of ground truth labels across physiological states (e.g., sleep stages) introduces label noise that differentially biases conformity scores by segment type.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Sleep stage scoring disagreement between raters is highest in N1/REM transitions; mislabeled segments receive incorrect conformity scores, distorting the calibration distribution for those stages.
cards.causal_path: Inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa per stage) -> label error rate -> conformity score contamination -> calibration quantile bias -> stage-specific coverage
cards.rival_explanation: Stage-specific coverage differences reflect true physiological non-stationarity, not label noise.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage error correlates with physiological variability metrics (e.g., HRV), not with kappa.
cards.distinguishing_test: Use only consensus-labeled epochs (kappa=1); if coverage differences persist, rival wins.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Typical sleep staging kappa 0.7-0.85; label error ~10-15% in transition epochs; conformity score bias scales with error rate.
cards.testable_prediction: N1 and REM stages show >5% coverage deviation from nominal when calibrated on all stages vs. consensus-only calibration.
cards.failure_condition: Coverage deviation unchanged when using consensus labels only.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Bootstrap coverage difference: all-labels calibration vs consensus-only calibration per stage; 95% CI excludes 0.
cards.falsification_test: Simulate label noise at observed kappa levels on clean data; if simulated coverage pattern doesn't match real data, label noise insufficient.

cards.hypothesis: Improper stratification by physiological state during calibration set construction leads to under-representation of rare but high-variability states (e.g., arrhythmia episodes), causing conditional coverage failure.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Random temporal splits place rare high-variability states predominantly in test set; calibration quantiles estimated from common low-variability states are too narrow for rare states.
cards.causal_path: State prevalence (arrhythmia burden %) -> calibration set state representation -> conformity score quantile estimation error -> conditional coverage gap
cards.rival_explanation: Conditional coverage failure is due to inherent unpredictability of arrhythmia, not calibration set composition.
cards.rival_prediction: Even with stratified calibration, arrhythmia segments show under-coverage due to fundamental noise.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage with stratified vs random calibration; stratified should close gap if H6 true.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Rare states (<5% prevalence) can have 2-3x conformity score dispersion; random splits often yield <10 calibration samples.
minimum_data_needed: Long recordings with annotated rare states
cards.testable_prediction: Stratified calibration reduces arrhythmia segment coverage gap from >15% to <3% vs random calibration.
cards.failure_condition: Stratified calibration does not significantly improve rare-state coverage (p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: McNemar test on coverage indicators (covered/not) for rare-state segments under two calibration schemes.
cards.falsification_test: Generate synthetic data where rare state has same conformity distribution as common state; stratified calibration should not help.

cards.hypothesis: Violation of exchangeability due to strong temporal autocorrelation in conformity scores causes the effective calibration sample size to be much smaller than nominal, inflating coverage variance across segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: High autocorrelation (AR(1) coefficient >0.8) in conformity scores means adjacent segments provide little independent information; the effective degrees of freedom for quantile estimation is reduced, widening the quantile confidence interval.
cards.causal_path: Conformity score AR(1) coefficient -> effective sample size (n_eff) -> quantile estimation variance -> coverage variance across test segments
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage variance is driven by true physiological non-stationarity, not statistical dependence.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage variance persists after pre-whitening conformity scores.
cards.distinguishing_test: Apply block bootstrap vs i.i.d. bootstrap for quantile CI; if block bootstrap CI captures coverage variance better, H7 supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: AR(1)=0.85 reduces n_eff to ~15% of nominal; quantile CI width scales with 1/sqrt(n_eff).
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage variance across segments exceeds i.i.d. binomial variance by factor >3 when AR(1)>0.8.
cards.failure_condition: Observed coverage variance matches i.i.d. binomial prediction after accounting for segment count.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Chi-square test: observed coverage variance vs expected under i.i.d. binomial; Levene's test for variance equality across AR(1) strata.
cards.falsification_test: Phase-randomized conformity scores (preserving spectrum, destroying temporal structure); if coverage variance drops to i.i.d. level, autocorrelation is causal.

cards.hypothesis: Segment-specific motion artifact distributions create heterogeneous noise floors that shift conformity score distributions in a state-dependent manner, unaccounted for by standard calibration.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Walking produces broadband EMG contamination increasing high-frequency power; this inflates morphology-based nonconformity scores during activity, but calibration on mixed states yields quantiles that are too wide for rest and too narrow for vigorous activity.
cards.causal_path: Activity level (accelerometer VMU) -> EMG contamination power (20-50 Hz) -> morphology feature distortion -> nonconformity score inflation -> activity-stratified coverage bias
cards.rival_explanation: Activity-related coverage changes reflect true physiological HRV changes with exercise, not artifact.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage bias correlates with HRV metrics, not EMG power, after controlling for activity level.
cards.distinguishing_test: In matched HRV bins, test if residual coverage bias correlates with EMG power.
cards.effect_size_rationale: EMG can exceed ECG amplitude 5-10x during vigorous activity; morphology features highly sensitive to high-frequency contamination.
cards.testable_prediction: High-activity segments (VMU>100) show >20% over-coverage; low-activity (VMU<10) show >10% under-coverage with pooled calibration.
cards.failure_condition: Activity-stratified coverage bias <2% after EMG power regression.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-way ANOVA: coverage ~ activity_stratum * calibration_method (pooled vs stratified); interaction term test.
cards.falsification_test: Clean ECG + synthetic EMG at measured levels; if coverage pattern matches real data, artifact mechanism sufficient.

cards.hypothesis: Calibration set contamination by undetected pathological beats (e.g., PVCs) biases conformity score quantiles, causing systematic over-coverage in clean segments and under-coverage in PVC-rich segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Undetected PVCs in calibration set have extreme morphology, inflating the upper quantile of conformity scores; this widens intervals globally, wasting efficiency on normal segments while still under-covering true PVC segments due to distributional shift.
cards.causal_path: PVC prevalence in calibration -> conformity score 95th percentile inflation -> global interval widening -> normal segment over-coverage + PVC segment residual under-coverage
control_variables: Automated PVC detection with manual verification
Exclude segments with >5% PVCs from calibration
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage pattern reflects true heterogeneity in prediction difficulty, not calibration contamination.
cards.rival_prediction: Removing PVCs from calibration does not change coverage pattern; PVC segments remain hard to predict.
cards.distinguishing_test: Re-calibrate after PVC removal; if normal segment coverage drops toward nominal and PVC coverage improves, H9 supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Single PVC can have conformity score >99th percentile of normal beats; 2% PVC contamination shifts 95th percentile substantially.
minimum_data_needed: Segment-level coverage for normal and PVC-rich segments
cards.testable_prediction: PVC-free calibration reduces normal segment coverage from 98% to 91% (nominal 90%) and improves PVC segment coverage from 70% to 85%.
cards.failure_condition: Coverage pattern unchanged after PVC removal from calibration set.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired comparison of coverage before/after PVC removal for normal and PVC segments; equivalence test for normal segments at 90%.
cards.falsification_test: Inject synthetic PVCs into clean calibration set at varying rates; if coverage pattern doesn't match observed, contamination not primary driver.

cards.hypothesis: Non-stationary noise covariance structure across physiological states (e.g., sleep vs wake) violates the conformal assumption of exchangeable residuals, causing state-conditional coverage failure even with marginally valid coverage.
cards.proposed_mechanism: During REM sleep, muscle atonia reduces EMG noise but increases respiratory sinus arrhythmia amplitude, changing the covariance of prediction residuals; conformity scores computed on wake residuals misestimate REM quantiles.
cards.causal_path: Physiological state (REM vs wake) -> residual covariance matrix (eigenvalues) -> Mahalanobis nonconformity score distribution -> state-conditional coverage
cards.rival_explanation: State-conditional coverage failure is due to mean shift in residuals, not covariance change.
cards.rival_prediction: Centering residuals per state eliminates coverage gap; covariance weighting unnecessary.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage using state-specific covariance vs state-specific mean only; covariance method should close gap if H10 true.
cards.effect_size_rationale: REM reduces EMG variance ~80% but increases RSA variance ~200%; Mahalanobis distance sensitive to eigenvalue ratios.
cards.testable_prediction: Wake-calibrated conformal predictor shows REM coverage <80% (nominal 90%); state-specific covariance calibration restores to 88-92%.
cards.failure_condition: State-specific mean adjustment alone achieves nominal REM coverage.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Likelihood ratio test: conformal model with state-specific covariance vs state-specific mean only; coverage binomial test per state.
cards.falsification_test: Generate residuals from state-specific Gaussian with matched means but pooled covariance; if coverage gap persists, covariance not the mechanism.
